method: Complete candidate survey followed by individual editorial choices and written reasons, applied to the existing complete guide to keep it within 300 quotations. All verified authorized selections included. Priority given to foundational teachings, substantive explanations, necessary qualifications, distinctive applications, narrative examples and thematic breadth across the betterment of the world as the purpose of every life, a concern embracing all people, practical care that protects dignity, service as worship, education and useful work, peace and honest public action, pure intention, humility and sacrifice, the purpose of revelation through history, shared hope and prayer, and communities learning to act together for social and economic development. Neither citation count nor source order used as a ranking rule. Imported wording checked separately; version differences remain explicit. The existing reading arc is retained.

selected.text: If a soul is interested in humanitarian deeds, his joy is perennial.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: if a soul is interested in humanitarian deeds, his joy is perennial; joy as the fruit of service.

selected.text: The love of humanity is a glittering generality without social service; … Social service is a mere catch-word without sacrifice and severance
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that love of humanity is a glittering generality without social service, and social service a catch-word without sacrifice; a necessary qualification.

selected.text: Arise with wisdom to serve the Cause of your Lord Who hath come for the betterment of the world and the unity of nations.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh: arise with wisdom to serve the Cause of your Lord Who hath come for the betterment of the world and unity of nations; links service and the Cause.

selected.text: There is no such thing as self-development. Growth only comes by working for others.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: there is no such thing as self-development; growth only comes by working for others; links inner growth with service.

selected.text: The Baha'is must be the servants of universal Peace, the workers for the Cause of the Oneness of the world of humanity, the spreaders of heavenly Love amongst the children of men, the promulgators of the principles of the progress of mankind, the dispellers of the clouds of religious, national, patriotic and political prejudices and the upholders of the inviolable rights of equality between men and women. They must correspond religious ideals with the deductions of science and reason and discard all such theories which cannot stand the test of intellect and empirical knowledge
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing Bahá’ís as servants of universal peace, dispellers of prejudice and upholders of equality between men and women; a broad social programme.

selected.text: This Wronged One appeared in days when naught remained of justice save a name and of equity save a trace. We summoned all to praiseworthy character and goodly deeds. Every fair-minded one beareth witness that this Wronged One hath had and hath no purpose except the reformation of the world and the edification of the souls of nations.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh: this Wronged One appeared when justice remained only as a name and has no purpose but the reformation of the world; a foundational declaration of purpose.

selected.text: Occupy not the days of your lives with the betterment of your own affairs; arise, rather, for the betterment of the world.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: This Wronged One hath at all times summoned the people unto truth and hath had no purpose except the reformation of God's servants and the edification of the world.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh: this Wronged One has summoned people to truth with no purpose but the reformation of God’s servants; purpose stated through the summons.

selected.text: Man is great; his aspiration too must be great in reforming the world and bringing comfort to nations
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh: man is great and his aspiration too must be great in reforming the world and bringing comfort to nations; links human dignity to the scale of service.

selected.text: Hold fast unto wisdom and cleave unto the betterment of the world and the refinement of the souls of nations.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh: hold fast unto wisdom and cleave unto the betterment of the world; wisdom as the manner of service.

selected.text: He will enlist himself in the army of human progress, to realize the limitless advancement of the human race.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on enlisting in the army of human progress for the limitless advancement of the human race; progress as a spiritual aim.

selected.text: in thanksgiving for this confirmation and success, protection and bounty of the Glorious Lord, the beloved of God must strive with perfect wisdom to strengthen the foundations of the Cause of God, establish and promote the Law of God, diffuse the fragrances of God, exalt the Word of God, advance souls in all degrees of existence, educate children, teach beneficial arts to youth, progress in the stages of civilization, multiply national industries, promote commerce, improve agriculture, spread knowledge, educate women, honor the leaves, care for the handmaidens of the Merciful, create love and unity among the friends, serve the government, show loyalty to the throne of sovereignty, wish well
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s long list of duties including educating children, teaching arts to youth, improving agriculture and educating women; a distinctive programme of social progress.

selected.text: We beseech God to ever aid His loved ones to that which will lead to the reformation of the world and the tranquility of the nations.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer that His loved ones be aided toward the reformation of the world and tranquility of nations; prayer for service.

selected.text: Man must strive and make an effort in the advancement of the ideals of justice, Universal civilization and the betterment of the conditions of the public.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: man must strive in the advancement of justice, universal civilization and the betterment of the public; joins justice and progress.

selected.text: Through justice commerce thrives, industries are developed, morals are refined, honesty is established, international comity fostered and education popularized.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: through justice commerce thrives, morals are refined and education is popularized; links justice to social progress.

selected.text: That which hath been made manifest in this Most Great Revelation is a mighty cause for the reformation of the world and the refinement of the souls of all peoples.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh: this Most Great Revelation is a mighty cause for the reformation of the world and the refinement of souls; joins social and personal reform.

selected.text: These teachings of the Ancient Beauty, which are the foundation of the progress of the world's peoples and the ladder of ascent for nations and peoples, must be implemented
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: the teachings are the foundation of the progress of peoples and must be implemented; links revelation and action.

selected.text: Our duty is to promote the manifest light - that is, we should pursue whatever leads to human perfections and virtues and the comfort and tranquility of the world of existence
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: our duty is to pursue whatever leads to human perfections and the tranquility of the world; a concise statement of duty.

selected.text: Therefore let us strive, so that we may spread divine Civilization, so that we may unfurl the Ensign of Knowledge so that we may illumine the minds, so that we may enlighten the intellects.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calling for the spread of divine civilization and the illumining of minds; joins civilization and knowledge.

selected.text: The basis of God's perfect laws is love for humanity and help for human needs. If all people followed this Revelation, the masses would be immeasurably uplifted and the Cause of God glorified.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: the basis of God’s laws is love for humanity and help for human needs; a foundational explanation.

selected.text: We have desired naught but the salvation of nations and the betterment of the world, yet the people turned away from Us and committed that which caused the pillars of the Primal Word to be dispersed.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh: We desired naught but the salvation of nations, yet the people turned away; purpose amid opposition.

selected.text: He must be the Establisher of Universal Civilization; the Unifier of religions, the standard-bearer of universal Peace and the embodiment of all the highest and noblest virtues of the world of humanity
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on the One Who must be the Establisher of Universal Civilization and the standard-bearer of universal peace; the Manifestation as world reformer.

selected.text: I swear by the grace of the Greatest Name that if souls would arise as they should, in a brief time the face of the earth would become the supreme paradise and this dusty heap would become the Abha Paradise
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá swearing that if souls would arise as they should the earth would become the Abhá Paradise; hope for transformation.

selected.text: May they arise to fulfill the divine teachings and contemplate peace and reconciliation with all the peoples of the world. May each become a kind servant to the human world and a loving friend to all humanity.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praying that the friends contemplate peace with all peoples and become kind servants to the human world; peace in personal relations.

selected.text: Rather, they should strive for the refinement and education of people, the guidance of nations, kindness and love between peoples, the connection of the human world, human unity, and universal comfort and tranquility.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: strive for the refinement of people, the guidance of nations and universal tranquility; a summary of the aims of public action.

selected.text: Baha'u'llah revealed heavenly teachings that will reform the phenomenal world, the world of spirits and hearts, the world of thought and capacity, the world of religion and philosophy. Verily the revelation of Baha'u'llah will reform all that pertains to man
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: Bahá’u’lláh’s teachings will reform all that pertains to man; the scope of revelation’s reform.

selected.text: Strive and make an effort so that this human world may achieve mighty progress in all degrees, even at the center of the earth, may show forth wondrous signs, and may become, in all aspects of perfection, the manifestation of the glorious signs of the All-Glorious
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: strive that this human world may achieve mighty progress in all degrees; a call to material and spiritual advancement.

selected.text: In this century of light precede all others in sympathy, in philanthropic actions, in physical and intellectual culture and in association with the rest of mankind. … Do not let the pool of your thoughts become stagnant. Open the shutters of your mind and air its secret chambers
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to young Bahá’ís urging them to lead in philanthropy and culture and to open the shutters of their minds; joins service to intellectual freedom.

selected.text: rather engage in educating the nation's children, promote sciences and knowledge, strive to improve morals, raise the banner of the oneness of humanity, lift up the call of human equality, remove the foundation of war and strife, and adorn the edifice of peace and reconciliation.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá urging education of the nation’s children, improvement of morals and removal of the foundation of war; public action through education.

selected.text: Therefore you must strive day unto day that the sun of Love may dawn from your hearts; day unto day the attractions of your consciousness may develop; day unto day you may become more loving to humanity, day unto day establish more rapid means of communication between the children of men.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: day unto day become more loving and establish more rapid means of communication between peoples; continual growth in service.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: strive that morals be transformed, hatred destroyed and the oneness of mankind adorned; moral reform as service.

selected.text: God hath created you for the betterment of the world.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh addressing the reader directly: God hath created you for the betterment of the world; makes the founding claim personal.

selected.text: I beseech God to make the world one region and one homeland, as has been revealed in the Tablets from the heaven of His Will, and to grant His servants the ability to occupy themselves with the betterment of the world and the refinement of their own souls, so that the light of knowledge may encompass all possibility.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer that the world become one homeland and His servants be occupied with its betterment and the refinement of their souls; joins outward and inward work.

selected.text: Direct all your thoughts to the progress of all, strive for the betterment of the condition of all souls and the refinement of character, and become endowed with divine attributes.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: direct all thoughts to the progress of all and the refinement of character; joins social progress and personal virtue.

selected.text: Most are unaware of the intention of this Wronged One and His loved ones, for were they to become cognizant they would testify that there hath been no purpose save the betterment, elevation and advancement of the servants.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh: were people aware of the intention of this Wronged One and His loved ones, they would testify to its purpose of betterment; purpose amid misunderstanding.

selected.text: If you are eager to serve God, serve mankind.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: if you are eager to serve God, serve mankind; the most concise statement of service as devotion.

selected.text: They must be the means of the happiness and progress of the world.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: they must be the means of the happiness and progress of the world; a concise call to shared progress.

selected.text: My hope is that you will all be enabled to serve the world of humanity unitedly.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s hope that all will be enabled to serve the world of humanity unitedly; service as a common undertaking.

selected.text: They desire service to the world of humanity. Therefore they are free from every bond.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on those who desire service to humanity and are therefore free from every bond; connects service with inner freedom.

selected.text: I hope that you will be under the protection of God, will succeed in rendering service to humanity and will always be a source of happiness to every heart.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hoping the listeners will render service to humanity and be a source of happiness to every heart; joins service with joy.

selected.text: Service to humanity is service to God. Let the love and light of the Kingdom radiate through you until all who look upon you shall be illumined by its reflection
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: God has created you for admonition, exhortation, the readjustment of morality, the illumination and the spiritualization of the world of humanity. This is your duty.

selected.text: that each one of you may become a resplendent sign, a banner in the Abha Kingdom, the cause of love and of amity among all men and serviceable to the world of Humanity
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: may each become the cause of amity among all men and serviceable to the world of humanity; a prayerful hope for service.

selected.text: I hope that God will assist you to serve all humanity without distinction between sects and religions, but rather to treat all according to the teachings of Baha'u'llah
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s hope that the friends will serve all humanity without distinction between sects and religions; names religious difference as no limit to service.

selected.text: Seek the well-being of all horizons and strive for the comfort of all who dwell on earth. Be the cause of gladness to the world of humanity and the means of prosperity for the servants of God
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking the friends to seek the well-being of all horizons and be the means of prosperity for God’s servants; extends care to all who dwell on earth.

selected.text: but rather spent their time in supplication and prayer, turning to the glorious Kingdom, striving for the good of all, serving humanity, experiencing spiritual attractions and divine inspirations
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing souls who spent their time in prayer while striving for the good of all and serving humanity; joins prayer and service.

selected.text: be a great bounty for the people of the world, and show love and kindness to humankind to the extent possible. … Day and night their thoughts should be confined to guiding humanity and educating souls
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: show love to humankind and let thoughts be confined to guiding humanity and educating souls; joins kindness and education.

selected.text: Perchance the friends of God may become the cause of humanity's salvation and the means of extinguishing the fire of hatred that has ever been and continues to be ablaze in the hearts of the world's peoples.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh hoping the friends become the means of extinguishing the fire of hatred in the hearts of the world’s peoples; carries the purpose to the believers.

selected.text: Therefore you must become so enkindled that you will banish all lethargy from the world of existence. Make the world a different world and cause humanity to receive bounties from the Most Great and Glorious One.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: become so enkindled as to banish lethargy and make the world a different world; a call to transforming zeal.

selected.text: They must be truthful and kind to all the peoples of the world, deal with all humanity with pure intent, absolute benevolence and heartfelt love, be sincere and well-wishing toward all the governments of the world
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: be truthful and kind to all peoples and sincere and well-wishing toward all governments; frames relations with governments.

selected.text: Thus will people offer service to one another with all their hearts for the sake of God and in order to fulfill the duties of devotion to Him and service to humanity and not for the purpose of acquiring praise and fame.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on service offered for God and not for praise and fame; reinforces the caution about recognition.

selected.text: I hope that through God's bounty thou wilt become ever more near to the divine threshold and successful in serving the Cause of God … to render outstanding services, and to leave an eternal trace in the world of humanity
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hoping the reader will render outstanding services and leave an eternal trace in the world of humanity; the lasting effect of service.

selected.text: If thou desirest to be confirmed in the service of the Kingdom of God, live in accord with the Teachings of Baha'u'llah and that is; - real love for the world of humanity and the utmost of kindness for the believers of God.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá linking confirmation in service to real love for the world of humanity and kindness to the believers; shows service to all and care for the community together.

selected.text: You are indeed a servant to humanity. A servant to humanity is a servant to God. Your mission is a high, holy and sanctified one; there could be no greater, no holier mission than that of bringing peace to this warring world.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to a peace worker: a servant to humanity is a servant to God, and no mission is holier than bringing peace; a narrative example.

selected.text: which has labored in the Cause of education are ever blessed. I am pleased with your hands. I love such hands very much, because they have worked for the children. May thou become a great educator and guide to humanity
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá blessing hands that have worked for the children in the cause of education; a narrative example of service through teaching.

selected.text: Jinab-i-Amin offers utmost praise for your outstanding services, that praise be to God, you are succeeding with perfect strength in servitude to the Threshold of the Divine Unity and are benevolent toward all humanity from every direction.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá conveying praise for outstanding services and benevolence toward all humanity; encouragement of service already rendered.

selected.text: This is worship: to serve mankind and to minister to the needs of the people. Service is prayer. A physician ministering to the sick, gently, tenderly, free from prejudice and believing in the solidarity of the human race, he is giving praise

selected.text: Let all the peace workers gather together their scattered forces and combine their material and moral resources. They must look forward and not backward, up and not down. They are the real benefactors of humanity, the burning torches of bright hope.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calling peace workers to combine their material and moral resources; cooperation with others working for peace.

selected.text: All humanity must obtain a livelihood by the sweat of the brow and bodily exertion, at the same time seeking to lift the burden of others, striving to be a source of comfort to souls and to facilitate their means of living. This in itself is devotion to God.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on earning a livelihood while lifting the burden of others, calling this in itself devotion to God; joins work, service and worship.

selected.text: If the object is to promote the public good, then the president must be a well-wisher of all and not a self-seeking person. If the object, however, is to promote personal interests, then such a position will be injurious to humanity and not beneficial to the public.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá testing public office by whether it serves the public good or personal interest; the guide’s test of honest office.

selected.text: What befits the servants of the Blessed Beauty is to serve all humanity and strive to spread universal peace, to raise the banner of harmony and lay the foundation of friendship, to lift up the call of truth-worship and become the cause of fellowship and unity among all peoples.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: what befits the servants of the Blessed Beauty is to serve all humanity and spread universal peace; joins service and peace.

selected.text: Be the cause of freedom for captives and the source of joy and happiness for the poor. Become divine healing for the sick and spiritual medicine for the ailing. Be a salve for every wound and a remedy for every pain. Be a bright candle and spread light in the gathering of humanity.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking the friends to free captives, bring joy to the poor and be a salve for every wound; vivid images of practical mercy.

selected.text: I have brought the message of Baha'u'llah to this country in order to teach people to investigate truth, to render service to humanity, to endeavor to bring about international peace, to exert every effort to guide humanity, to show kindness to all creatures and to raise the Call of the Kingdom.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá summarizing his purpose in America: to investigate truth, serve humanity and bring about international peace; a statement of mission.

selected.text: that they may treat all humanity with utmost truthfulness and love, both in private and in public, becoming a refuge for the fearful, a haven for those who cry for help, physicians to the sick, supporters of the lowly among men, sweet crystal water for the thirsty, a heavenly feast for the hungry
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on treating all with truthfulness and love and being a refuge for the fearful and a feast for the hungry; returns to concrete care at the close.

selected.text: Beseech thou God that thou mayest adopt a religion that is heart-appealing and sweet, which is the essence of the manifest Faith. selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on a heart-appealing religion whose essence is to become a mercy from the Lord and bestow life on humanity through word and deed; defines religion through service.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on having no interference in affairs except giving counsel and educating humanity; a necessary qualification on public involvement.

selected.text: I hope that you will ever strive for the good of all humanity and render outstanding service to mankind, that you will endure every hardship and difficulty in this path, and that you will succeed in manifesting such character and conduct and speech that you may become a luminous lamp in the assemblage of humanity.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hoping the reader will endure every hardship in serving all humanity and become a luminous lamp; perseverance in service.

selected.text: let us treat all people with divine attributes, and let us guide all humanity to the path of salvation and prosperity. selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: let us treat all people with divine attributes and be a healing balm for every wound; closes the linked readings with care for all.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calling these acts of sustenance, shelter and kindness to friend and stranger the attributes of the Bahá’ís; ties practical service to identity.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking that the reader’s brother, in any government post, serve with truthfulness and honesty and be content with his salary; a practical example of honest administration.

selected.text: We hope that the friends of God and handmaidens of the Merciful will, in accordance with heavenly teachings, serve the unity of the human world, consider religion as the foundation of love and fellowship among humanity, and strive to reconcile religion and science. selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hoping the friends will reconcile religion and science and become a treasure for every poor one; joins unity, knowledge and relief.

selected.text: No matter what lack of courtesy or what severe persecution or stern expressions of hate and unfathomable enmity you receive, you must have no excuse like the following: "So and so has spoken unkindly about me," "So and so has not done me justice,"--nay, rather you must have no excuse but live according to the Divine Teachings, whether humanity prove agreeable or disagreeable, whether humanity prove hateful or loving, whether it receives you or casts you out
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: whatever persecution or hate you receive, have no excuse but live according to the teachings; perseverance through hostility.

selected.text: To cheer up and sympathise with those who are in sorrow and carry laughter and the sunbeams of happiness in the hearts of all the children of humanity. selected.text: From the beginning of His stupendous mission, Baha'u'llah urged upon the attention of nations the necessity of ordering human affairs in such a way as to bring into being a world unified in all the essential aspects of its life. In unnumbered verses and tablets He repeatedly and variously declared the "progress of the world" and the "development of nations" as being among the ordinances of God for this day. The oneness of mankind, which is at once the operating principle and ultimate goal of His Revelation, implies the achievement of a dynamic coherence between the spiritual and practical requirements of life on earth. The indispensability of this coherence is unmistakably illustrated in His ordination of the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar, the spiritual centre of every Baha'i community round which must flourish dependencies dedicated to the social, humanitarian, educational and scientific advancement of mankind. Thus, we can readily appreciate that although it has hitherto been impracticable for Baha'i institutions generally to emphasize development activities, the concept of social and economic development is enshrined in the sacred Teachings of our Faith.

selected.text: As long as there will be life on earth, there will also be suffering, in various forms and degrees. But suffering, although an inescapable reality, can nevertheless be utilized as a means for the attainment of happiness. This is the interpretation given to it by all the Prophets and saints, who, in the midst of severe tests and trials, felt happy and joyous and experienced what is best and holiest in life. Suffering is both a reminder and a guide. It stimulates us to better adapt ourselves to our environmental conditions, and thus leads the way to self-improvement. In every suffering one can find a meaning and a wisdom. It is sometimes only when all our suffering has passed that we become aware of its usefulness. What man considers to be evil turns often to be a cause of infinite blessings. And this is due to his desire to know more than he can. God's wisdom is, indeed, inscrutable to us all, and it is no use pushing too far trying to discover that which shall always remain a mystery to our mind.
